Title: model-router prod default flips secret resolution from Key Vault to environment variables
Description:
Current behaviour: services/model-router/src/Api/appsettings.json (the only config file shipped for model-router — there is no appsettings.Production.json) sets "KeyResolver": {"Provider": "Env"}. services/model-router/src/Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs (lines ~38-44) selects EnvProviderKeyResolver for any Provider value other than exactly "KeyVault". Terraform (deploy/modules/container-apps/main.tf) injects KeyVault__Uri as an env var for model-router but never sets KeyResolver__Provider, and no GitHub Actions workflow sets it either (verified via grep — zero matches for KeyResolver, GEMINI_API_KEY, MODEL_ROUTER_ in .github/workflows/).
Expected behaviour: Production model-router must resolve provider API keys from Azure Key Vault by default, as it always has. "Env" resolution should only ever be active in the local preview stack (deploy/local/docker-compose.preview.yml / .env.preview), never as the committed production default.
Affected files: services/model-router/src/Api/appsettings.json:76-77 (KeyResolver.Provider); services/model-router/src/Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:38-44
Impact: Every model-router call in production (Foundry, Anthropic, and Gemini) throws "No API key configured for '<secret>'" because EnvProviderKeyResolver looks for environment variables that Container Apps never sets — Key Vault secrets are provisioned but silently bypassed. This breaks the entire model-router service in production.
ReproSteps:
1. Deploy model-router to Azure Container Apps using the current committed appsettings.json and Terraform in deploy/.
2. Observe that KeyResolver:Provider resolves to "Env" (no override exists anywhere in Terraform or CI).
3. Call any model-router completion endpoint.
4. EnvProviderKeyResolver.ResolveAsync throws InvalidOperationException("No API key configured for ...") because required env vars (e.g. MODEL_ROUTER_FOUNDRY_API_KEY) are not set in the Container App's environment — only KEYVAULT_URI is.
Discussion:
FINDING: model-router prod default silently flips secret resolution from Key Vault to environment variables. The root cause is that appsettings.json (the only config file shipped — there is no appsettings.Production.json) sets KeyResolver.Provider to "Env" instead of "KeyVault". While the DI registration in DependencyInjection.cs correctly selects EnvProviderKeyResolver unless Provider is exactly "KeyVault", the Container Apps deployment never overrides this default value via environment configuration. Fix: Revert the default in appsettings.json to "KeyVault"; keep "Env" only as an override in deploy/local/docker-compose.preview.yml / .env.preview for the local preview stack.
RESOLUTION: Instead of a static default string, DependencyInjection.cs now auto-detects: KeyResolver:Provider empty (default) + KeyVault:Uri set -> KeyVaultProviderKeyResolver; KeyVault:Uri empty -> EnvProviderKeyResolver. Explicit "Env"/"KeyVault" override still works. This matches the KeyVault:Uri-presence convention already used by every other service in the fleet (identity, job-orchestrator, api-gateway, evidence, ingestion), so prod (Terraform sets KeyVault__Uri) resolves via Key Vault with no Terraform/CI change needed, and local preview (KeyVault:Uri left empty) resolves via env vars. appsettings.json KeyResolver.Provider reverted to "" (auto). Verified: dotnet build 0 errors, 171 tests pass.
